title: Zanchi: generic living/dead split — then a stricter fiducia in the promises
source_text: XIV. Similiter fides Zanchio definitur, Virtus a Deo nobis donata, qua quicquid propositum olim fuit nomine Dei a Prophetis & Apostolis, nunc autem nobis ex ipsorum scriptis praedicatur, persuasi sumus esse Verbum Dei, illudque totum, tam legem, quam Evangelium ut certum Dei verbum credimus ac profitemur. Tom. 4. lib. 1. cap. 12. de Fide, Thesi prima. Sed haec definitio fidei ipsi generica est. Nam postea Thesi secunda fidem sic definitam dividit in vivam & mortuam. Vivam, quae per dilectionem efficax est, & profert opera pietatis. Mortuam, quae hac efficacitate destituta est. Cum autem fides viva, & fides justificans sint reapse unum & idem, quandoquidem omnis fides justificans viva est, & vicissim omnis fides viva est justificans, inde videtur facile confici posse, ex doctrina Zanchii, vera definitio fidei justificantis. Nempe, si dicamus illam esse qua totum Dei Verbum, tam legem quam Evangelium, ut certum Dei verbum credimus ac profitemur, eo assensu qui sit per dilectionem efficax. Sed tamen in eodem & libro & capite, fidem justificantem aliter artius definit. Fides enim justificans ipsi est, Firmus & indubitatus assensus in promissiones Dei de remissione peccatorum, & justitia accipienda, aeternaque vita consequenda a Deo, per & propter filium Jesum Christum, ex afflatu Spiritus Sancti in nobis excitatus. Titulo De Fiducia, in Explicatione primae Theseos.
pass_a_gloss: Similarly faith is defined by Zanchi as a Virtue given to us by God by which we are persuaded that whatever was formerly proposed in God’s name by the Prophets and Apostles, and is now preached to us from their writings, is the Word of God, and we believe and profess that whole — both law and Gospel — as the sure word of God. Tom. 4, book 1, ch. 12 on Faith, first Thesis. But this definition of faith is for him generic. For afterward in the second Thesis he divides faith so defined into living and dead. Living, which is efficacious through love and brings forth works of piety. Dead, which is destitute of this efficacy. But since living faith and justifying faith are in very deed one and the same — seeing that every justifying faith is living, and in turn every living faith is justifying — thence a true definition of justifying faith seems easily able to be made from Zanchi’s doctrine. Namely, if we say it is that by which we believe and profess the whole Word of God, both law and Gospel, as the sure word of God, with that assent which is efficacious through love. Yet in the same book and chapter he defines justifying faith otherwise more narrowly. For justifying faith for him is a Firm and undoubted assent to God’s promises concerning remission of sins, and justice to be received, and eternal life to be obtained from God, through and for the sake of the Son Jesus Christ, excited in us by the breathing of the Holy Spirit. Under the title On Trust, in the Explanation of the first Thesis.
pass_b_english: Zanchi’s broad definition: God-given virtue persuading us the whole preached Word is God’s — law and Gospel.
He splits that into living (love-efficacious) and dead.
Living = justifying; so justifying faith = Word-assent efficacious through love.
Narrower later: firm undoubted assent to promises of remission, justice, eternal life in Christ — Spirit-excited fiducia.
